trial_court: Additional District Judge, 11th Court, Alipore, Matrimonial Suit No. 6/1985
case_name: Sukhdev Kaur (Grewal) v. Ravinder Singh Grewal
facts_of_case: The parties are Sikh by religion and were married according to Sikh rites and ceremonies in 1970. The husband filed for divorce on grounds of desertion and cruelty. The wife refused to accompany the husband to his posting at Doomdooma, stayed only two months, and then started living with her parents. She also joined a B.Ed. course against the husband's wishes.

legal_principles.principle: Unsubstantiated allegations of cheating, criminal breach of trust or criminal misappropriation against a husband or his mother can constitute cruelty.
legal_principles.held: There is no doubt - and it can be noted as a general proposition - that unsubstantiated allegations of cheating, criminal breach of trust or criminal mis- appropriation against husband or against the mother of the husband and filing of criminal case on such unsubstantiated allegations would no doubt constitute cruelty on the part of the wife.
cited_cases: Sukhdev Kaur (Grewal) vs Ravinder Singh Grewal, 1996

legal_principles.principle: Filing a criminal case on unsubstantiated allegations is sure to cause humiliation and mental agony to the husband.
legal_principles.held: There is no gain-saying that filing of a criminal case on unsubstantiated allegations of offences of cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal misappropriation is sure to cause humiliation and mental agony to the husband.
cited_cases: Sukhdev Kaur (Grewal) vs Ravinder Singh Grewal, 1996

outcome.final_order: The trial court granted decree of divorce in favour of the petitioner-husband on grounds of cruelty of the wife. The appeal is allowed and the decree of divorce is set aside.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
